cues: When there are two different beta carbons, two alkenes are possible.
Two bromobutane can lose a hydrogen from either side.
Saytzeff's rule: the major product is the more substituted alkene, the one with more alkyl groups on the double bond, because it is more stable.
So but two ene is major.
The ease of elimination is tertiary, then secondary, then primary.
